memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. Do not go over your vineyard a second time or pick up the grapes that have fallen. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.'" - Lev 19:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most beautiful laws in the Bible. Do not harvest to the very edge. Do not go back for the grapes you missed. Leave them.

Think about what this means for a farmer. He is being told to deliberately take less than he could. Not to give away his profits afterwards, but to build the generosity into how he works in the first place.

And notice how it is designed. God does not tell the farmer to hand out food. He tells him to leave it in the field, so the poor can come and gather it themselves. Dignity is protected. The hungry person works for what they receive. They are not paraded as recipients of charity.

This is exactly how Ruth, a foreign widow with nothing, fed herself and Naomi — gleaning in Boaz's field (Ruth 2:2-3). And through that law, she met the man who would become her husband, and she entered the family line of Jesus.

The question for us is simple: what are the edges of your field? Not what you give away from your surplus, but what you deliberately do not take. Time you do not fill. Money you do not spend on yourself. Space you leave for others.

Generosity is not what is left over. It is planned.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are "the edges of your field" in your life?
2. Do you plan generosity, or only give from what happens to be left?
3. How can you help others in a way that protects their dignity?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You built care for the poor into ordinary work. Help me leave edges in my field — planned generosity that treats others with dignity. Amen.
